headline: Apple Vision Pro Exec Joining OpenAI's Hardware Team Amidst Leadership Shakeup
summary: Paul Meade, VP behind Apple's Vision Pro, is reportedly leaving to bolster OpenAI's hardware efforts, coinciding with internal leadership changes at Apple.
details: Paul Meade, the Apple vice president who oversaw the development of the Vision Pro headset, is reportedly leaving the tech giant to join OpenAI's hardware team. The move was reported by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.

Meade was also reportedly in charge of the AI-powered smart glasses that Apple is planning to release next year. While the Vision Pro faced a high price point and mixed reception, Apple aims for more affordable smart glasses to compete with rivals like Meta.

This departure is seen as a consequence of John Ternus's impending promotion to Apple CEO and his subsequent restructuring of the hardware engineering department, which has reportedly led to some vice presidents feeling demoted.

Meanwhile, OpenAI is collaborating with former Apple chief design officer Jony Ive on a new AI device. CEO Sam Altman has described it as a potentially more peaceful alternative to the iPhone, though reports last fall indicated challenges in finalizing the product's details.

headline: Anonymous GitHub user mass-drops undisclosed 0-days
summary: A GitHub repository has been created to archive previously undisclosed zero-day vulnerabilities and their proof-of-concept exploits.
details: An anonymous GitHub user has released a repository containing a consolidated archive of public proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits and vulnerability research writeups. The repository, named 'exploitarium', aims to preserve the contents of former standalone PoC repositories.

The user states that this sharing keeps them motivated to continue dropping their findings. The repository includes direct entries for various vulnerabilities, such as c-ares-tcp-uaf-calc-poc, ffmpeg-rasc-dlta-calc-poc, and libssh2-cve-2026-55200-poc, among others.

The consolidation was verified against fresh GitHub clones on June 23, 2026, ensuring that the tracked files in the new repository are identical to those in the original ones. This check covered 12 repos and 96 tracked entries with zero mismatches.

The creator emphasizes that the material in this repository should not be used maliciously. It is intended as good-faith, open-disclosure vulnerability research to encourage more interest in cybersecurity.
